# <a id="_3zaxaki5rj7e"></a>__The Conspiracy of the Three C’s: Cars, Computers and Cell Phones__

[JANET RILEY](https://substack.com/@juanita4141)

Jan 19, 2026

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

I have a theory that life is like a pinochle game: just when you think you’ve got a winning hand, the universe deals you a “mis\-deal\.” During my working years, before the quiet of retirement, these interruptions usually came from a trio of troublemakers I call the __Three C’s: Computers, Cars, and Cell Phones\.__ They seemed to coordinate their strikes for the sole purpose of keeping me humble and reminding me that life is an adventure I am not entirely in charge of\.

The __Computer__ was the first to revolt\. While I was still at my desk every day, my work email decided it was tired of the “automatic” life\. If I wanted to hear from a colleague or a client, I had to manually beg it to “Send and Receive\.” Then, it developed a strange form of digital gaslighting\. It would refuse to let me create a new folder for a project, claiming one already existed with that name—yet that folder was nowhere to be seen\.

The “fix” for this was even more of a test\. After technical support reset my settings, every email I had already read, answered, and deleted over the previous several months came screaming back from the dead like a digital haunting\. I spent hours of my workday sorting through the ghosts of projects past\. At one point, I wondered if I had made the fatal mistake of praying for patience, though I truly couldn’t recall being that reckless\.

Once the computer finally began to behave, the __Car__ decided it was its turn in the spotlight\.

I always kept my car maintained with the precision of a Swiss watch, but the “Three C’s” don’t care about your service records\. One Thursday night after a long day at the office, my car started, stalled, started, and stalled again—a mechanical “hissy fit” if I ever saw one\. After years of reliable service, I found myself waiting for a tow truck in the dark, eventually surrendering my keys for a loaner car just so I could get back to work the next morning\.

Now, I find myself looking suspiciously at my __Cell Phone__\. It’s the last of the trio, and I know it’s plotting something\. I’ve started manually writing down my appointments and backing up my contacts like I’m preparing for a digital hurricane\.

I’ve realized that you have to laugh at the Three C’s\. If you don’t, they win\. So, while I’m asking God for help to fix the mechanical bits or cope with the tech, I’m also asking for the sense of humor to realize that these “adventures” are just the price of admission for a life well\-lived\.
